MUQATIL:6:76-80/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r1.claim: At the end of the month Abraham sees Venus from a cave; its setting, then the setting of the larger, brighter moon and sun, proves that none is his enduring Lord, and he seeks guidance lest he stray.
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r1.anchor: دنا من باب السرب، وذلك فى آخر الشهر، فرأى الزهرة أول الليل من خلال السرب

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r38.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r38.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r38.claim: Abraham's plea for guidance indicates that only God guides and may expose his people's religious status.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r38.anchor: indicates, as in v. 71, that the only guidance is God’s guidance and it was perhaps meant to indicate to his people their own religious status (R)

TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r5.claim: The moon’s this is my lord repeats the earlier hypothetical or accommodating argument; after it sets, the conditional plea for guidance implies persistence would have made Abraham one of the deluded moon-worshippers.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#20/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الوضع الذي ذكره في القمر بقوله { هذا ربي } كان ضلالا لو دام وأصر عليه

THALABI:v4p163/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r2.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p163/r2.claim: One view takes Ibrahim’s statements at face value: he was a child before proof and guidance, when he was neither an unbeliever nor a believer.
THALABI:v4p163/r2.anchor: فأجراه بعضهم على الظاهر. وقالوا: ما كان إبراهيم (عليه السلام) مسترشدا متحيرا

THALABI:v4p163/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p163/r3.claim: In a report through Ali ibn Abi Talha, Ibn Abbas says Ibrahim worshipped the star, moon, and sun until each set, then asked for guidance and disavowed shirk.
THALABI:v4p163/r3.anchor: يدل عليه ما روى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: لما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا

THALABI:v4p163/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p163/r4.claim: Other scholars reject that account because a prophet cannot pass through a time without monotheism, knowledge, or disavowal of every other object of worship.
THALABI:v4p163/r4.anchor: وأنكر الآخرون هذا القول، وقالوا: غير جائز أن يكون لله عز وجل رسول

THALABI:v4p163/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p163/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p163/r6.claim: The first of four interpretations is that Ibrahim feigned agreement with star-worshippers to expose their error: setting revealed the celestial bodies’ incapacity, although his people revered and consulted them.
THALABI:v4p163/r6.anchor: الوجه الأول: أن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) أراد أن يستدرجهم بهذا القول ويعرفهم خطأهم

THALABI:v4p164/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r1.claim: A further interpretation treats ‘this is my lord’ as an argument from the opponents’ own assumptions: the star sets, and the moon is greater, so their worship is untenable.
THALABI:v4p164/r1.anchor: والوجه الثالث: أن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) قال هذا على وجه الاحتجاج على قومه لا على معنى الشك في ربه

THALABI:v4p164/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r2.claim: The account uses ellipsis: Ibrahim means ‘they say this is my lord’; as with the prayer after Abraham and Ishmael raised the House’s foundations.
THALABI:v4p164/r2.anchor: في الآية اختصار وإضمار ومعناها قال: يقولون هذا ربي كقوله وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت

THALABI:v4p164/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r3.claim: Ibrahim rejects a lord that disappears at setting, then repeats the argument for the moon and sun; the sun’s greater brightness makes its disappearance still clearer.
THALABI:v4p164/r3.anchor: فلما أفل غاب وزال قال: لا أحب الآفلين ربا، لا يدوم

ELMALILI:6:75-82/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r7.claim: Abraham repeats the same argumentative taunt when the moon rises, then says he would be among the misguided if his Lord did not guide him, confessing dependence on divine guidance and gratitude for it.
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r7.anchor: hem de her lahza rabbine olan ihtiyâcını itiraf ile hidâyetine şükretmek için

ELMALILI:6:75-82/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r8.claim: The statements “this is my Lord” are argumentative and ironic, not sincere affirmation; without a moment of divine guidance, humanity could mistake a transient object for the everlasting and fall into error.
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r8.anchor: هَٰذَا رَبِّى sözlerinin iltizâmî olmayıp ilzâmî ve inkârî olduğunu anlatmak

ELMALILI:6:75-82/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r9.claim: The moon’s beauty can readily captivate people; without God’s instant guidance, humanity in darkness would worship the moon, stars, or idols.
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r9.anchor: zulmetteki beşeriyet Ay’a da tapacak, yıldıza da tapacak, puta da tapacak.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: The reference to Abraham and later prophets asserts that they invited people to Muhammad’s same message; Muhammad must follow their guidance and leave rejecters to themselves, since he must preach but cannot force belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: His responsibility is to only preach and he is not liable to force people to accept guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Abraham is singled out because Israelites and Ishmaelites both claimed him as patriarch and guide while attributing their inherited religious practices to him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: both the Israelites and the Ishmaelites regarded him as their patriarch and spiritual leader.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Judaism, Christianity, and Ishmaelite polytheism are later fabrications with no connection to Abraham; Muhammad’s mission revives and completes Abraham’s religion for his descendants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: it was also essential to make it evident to the Ishmaelites that the religion of polytheism they have adopted is their own fabrication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p63/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p63/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p63/.claim: The account of Abraham’s observation of the star, moon, and sun expands the earlier brief statement: their submission to divine laws shows that only their Creator deserves worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p63/.anchor: they explain the brevity found in the previous verses. Previously, it was stated how Abraham (sws) exposed the hollow nature of the religion followed by his father and his nation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.claim: Prophets share a preaching purpose but adjust style to their audience and temperament; John and Jesus use parables, while other prophets may sermonize or use legal diction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.anchor: owing to the peculiar temperament and nature of their addressees, every prophet has some distinctive features with regard to his style of preaching and methodology of reasoning.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.claim: Abraham’s argumentative audience often refused to listen and quickly turned to polemics, so he used gradual reasoning to lead them into a position where they had no answer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.anchor: Abraham’s nation was very inclined to polemical debates and argumentation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.claim: The idol-smashing episode exemplifies Abraham’s method: he directed people to ask the surviving idol and its victims, eliciting their admission that idols cannot speak or defend themselves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.anchor: He also gestured towards the shattered idols and asked them to inquire from these victims because if they speak, they will narrate what calamity befell them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.claim: Abraham also used turiya: a true statement that can mislead listeners until his plan has unfolded; Islahi postpones its fuller example and lexical discussion to al-Saffat.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p64/.anchor: As per this device, in order to carry out his plan, he would give a statement that would be true but could potentially mislead his addressees.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.claim: Gradual reasoning and turiya may be punctuated with polite humor; light humor is also a prophetic trait, with examples to come in al-Anbiya and al-Saffat.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.anchor: light and polite humour is also a trait of prophets of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.claim: Abraham presents the Creator’s relation with worshippers as love rather than mere fear; fading heavenly objects are themselves subservient and cannot merit that love.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p65/.anchor: a person’s relationship with his creator and master is that of love and not mere fear.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.claim: The moon scene advances the lesson: worshipping things that fade is serious error, a cause for sorrow, and people depend on God alone for guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.anchor: What becomes further evident is that this error is not small. It is a matter of great sorrow and yearning.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.speaker: some exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.claim: Some exegetes take Abraham’s conditional statement about guidance as referring to the past; Islahi says this reading needlessly stretches the text.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.anchor: Some exegetes opine that this condition relates to the past

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.claim: Abraham’s words about needing guidance state a general truth and do not mean he was previously astray; he holds up his noble nature as a mirror to his people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p66/.anchor: Saying these words does not necessitate that Abraham (sws) was in error earlier or thought that he was in error.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: The author describes prophetic revelation as light upon light and refers readers to 24:35 for fuller discussion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: darkness but of light upon light.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Prophets begin by inviting their closest relatives; Abraham first invited his father before addressing his nation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: He first invited his father and this precisely has been the way of prophets of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Abraham's argument from the celestial kingdom came after his appointment: prophets first invite their closest relatives, then address their nation, and 6:79–80 speaks with prophetic authority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: The proof that this incident took place after Abraham (sws) was made a prophet is found in verses 79-80.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Treating the episode as an intellectual journey produces an illogical sequence: the small star appears first, while a cave story was invented to explain why Abraham saw Venus before the sun.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: A more illogical narrative had to be fabricated to justify this illogical sequence of observation:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Gradual argument accepts an opponent's premise to trap him, not to endorse it; Abraham uses the celestial bodies' setting to defeat their claim that their shining proves divinity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: if their shine is the proof of their divinity, then they should also witness their setting and fading away.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: Prophets use natural, context-sensitive methods including gradual reasoning, humor, sarcasm, and double meanings; an apparently affectionate pause or sarcasm can persuade beyond many arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: These include gradual reasoning, humour, sarcasm, using words and sentences with double-meaning etc.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p70/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p70/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p70/.claim: Using one's intellect and innate capacities lifts celestial bodies above idols made by human hands; neglecting them leads to worshipping carved rocks.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p70/.anchor: if a person does not use his intellect and innate abilities, he ends up prostrating before rocks he has carved out

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r3.claim: بزوغ is the first appearance or rising of a heavenly body.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p562/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p562/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p562/r14.claim: Abraham’s condemnation of idolatry proves his guidance: “this is my Lord” is a concession to the opponent, exposing the impossibility of a changing, setting body as deity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p562/r14.anchor: وهذا الإنكار من إبراهيم على أبيه والإخبار أنه وقومه في ضلال مبين أدل دليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r3.claim: Abraham did not wait for the first star to rise because stars become visible as night darkens; after rebutting it, he awaited the brighter moon and then sun to show they share its createdness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r3.anchor: أولا ما ارتقب حتى بزغ الكوكب لأنه بإظلام الليل تظهر الكواكب بخلاف حاله مع القمر والشمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r4.claim: The moon was seen at its first rising, and Abraham repeated the argument with the sun because it is brighter, larger, and more beneficial, yet likewise subject to change.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r4.anchor: ثم عمل كذلك في الشمس ارتقبها إذ كانت أنور من القمر وأضوأ وأكبر جرما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r5.claim: The lost people are worshipers of created beings; the verse is therefore used by some to argue that “this is my lord” was literal and occurred in childhood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r5.anchor: القوم الضالون هنا عبدة المخلوقات كالأصنام وغيرها واستدل بهذا من زعم أن قوله: هذا ربي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes Abraham’s plea for guidance as a warning that anyone who makes the setting moon divine is astray, since guidance depends on God’s enabling grace.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p565/r6.anchor: لئن لم يهدني ربي تنبيه لقومه على أن من اتخذ القمر إلها وهو نظير الكوكب في الأفول فهو ضال

BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r4.claim: The moon was beginning to rise after the star had set.
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r4.anchor: أي : مبتدئا في الطلوع إثر غروب الكوكب

BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r5.claim: Ibrahim’s plea for guidance indirectly tells his people that they are astray.

BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r6.claim: Bursevi supposes a high western mountain hid the star and moon around midday or shortly afterward, while the eastern horizon remained open.
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r6.anchor: ولعله عليه السلام كان إذ ذاك في موضع كان من جانبه الغربي جبل شامخ يستتر به الكواكب والقمر

BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r7.claim: That mountain and open horizon explain a sequence that otherwise seems scarcely possible: the moon rising after the star sets and setting before sunrise.
BURSEVI:v3p44#2/r7.anchor: وإلا فطلوع القمر بعد أفول الكوكب ثم أفوله قبل طلوع الشمس مما لا يكاد يتصور

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r8.claim: Moon worshipers bow to the rising moon, pictured as a silver tray at the edge of the green celestial table.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r8.anchor: ماه طبق سيمين بر كناره خوان سبز فلك نمودار شد

BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r9.claim: After the moon moves west of the meridian, Ibrahim asks for his Lord’s guidance rather than joining those who are astray.
BURSEVI:v3p46#3/r9.anchor: ازخط نصف النهار بجانب مغرب ميل كرد {قال لئن لم يهدنى ربى لاكونن من القوم الضآلين}

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r1.claim: Abraham, dated to around 2100 BCE and regarded as leader of the monotheistic Hanif tradition, lived among people who worshipped celestial bodies and their idol symbols.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r1.anchor: Milâttan önce 2100’lerde yaşadığı kabul edilen ve Allah’ın birliği esasına dayalı dinî geleneğin (Hanîflik) önderi olarak bilinen Hz. İbrâhim’in kavmi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r2.claim: According to the Torah, tablets found in excavations at Abraham's birthplace, Ur, mention about five thousand divine names.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r2.anchor: Tevrat’a göre Hz. İbrâhim’in doğum yeri olan Ur şehrinde yapılan kazılar sonucu bulunan tabletlerde 5000 civarında tanrı ismi geçmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r3.claim: Abraham was probably already a monotheist before these observations; he considered a star, then the moon and sun, to persuade his people from within their false beliefs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r3.anchor: muhtemelen kendisi bu gözlemlere girişmeden önce de tevhid ehlinden olmakla birlikte, kavminin bu bâtıl inançlarından hareket ederek onları tevhid akîdesine ikna etmek düşüncesiyle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r4.claim: His argument is that transient, changing beings cannot be gods or objects of divine love, so none of the celestial bodies is divine and only God is truly worthy of worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r4.anchor: gelip geçici ve değişken bir varlığın tanrı olamayacağı, tanrısal bir sevgiyle benimsenemeyeceği şeklindeki temel gerçeğe dayanarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r5.claim: Abraham's declaration of certain faith culminates in turning as a hanif to the Creator of heaven and earth and disavowing associationism; his observational reasoning refutes idolatry and demonstrates proper belief in God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r5.anchor: “Ben, Hanîf olarak yüzümü, gökleri ve yeri yoktan yaratana çevirdim ve ben müşriklerden değilim” ifadesiyle ortaya koymuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r8.claim: The Qur'an's main struggle is against associationism rather than outright atheism because it regards the idea of divinity as innate and corrupted by polytheism and other forms of shirk.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:76/r8.anchor: Kur’an’ın temel tavrı, tanrı tanımazlardan ziyade şirkle mücadeledir.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r1.claim: These readers open both vowels in رأى القمر and رأى الشمس when followed by a vowelless consonant; the same reading occurs in 18:53 and 16:86.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي وابن عامر: رأى القمر [الأنعام/ 77]

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r2.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r2.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim and Hamza break rāʾ while opening hamza throughout the Qur’an.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة: رأى القمر ورأى الشمس بكسر الراء وفتح الهمزة في كل القرآن

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r3.speaker: خلف عن يحيى بن آدم عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r3.claim: This transmission from Asim breaks both rāʾ and hamza in رأى القمر and رأى الشمس.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r3.anchor: وذكر خلف عن يحيى بن آدم عن أبي بكر عن عاصم: رأى القمر ورأى الشمس بكسر الراء والهمزة معا

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r4.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r4.claim: Hafs from Asim opens both rāʾ and hamza in رأى throughout the Qur’an.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r4.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم: بفتح الراء والهمزة في رأى* في كل القرآن .

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r5.claim: Al-Farisi rejects some of Ahmad’s companions’ description of both vowels as kasra: the hamza has imala of its fatha, not kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي: تحقيق هذا: وإمالة فتحة الهمزة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r6.claim: When the alif drops before a vowelless consonant, its imala and the preceding fatha’s inclination both disappear because the fatha had inclined the alif toward yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r6.anchor: فلما سقطت الألف بطلت إمالتها لسقوطها، ولما بطلت إمالتها لسقوطها بطلت إمالة الفتحة نحو الكسرة

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r7.claim: Readers who open rāʾ in رأى المجرمون after breaking it in رأى كوكبا preserve two accepted language forms; opening also follows رمى and رعى, while hamza imala can affect rāʾ as well.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r7.anchor: آثروا الأخذ باللغتين، كسر الراء وفتحها، فكسرها لما ذكر، وفتحها لأنهم جعلوها بمنزلة الراء في رمى ورعى

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r8.claim: Kasra on rāʾ can be an independent morphological effect, separate from hamza imala, so a reader need not use imala to apply it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p329/r8.anchor: فلأن كسر الراء إنما هو للتنزيل الذي ذكرنا، وهو معنى منفصل من إمالة فتحة الهمزة

QASHANI:6:76-77/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:76-77/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:76-77/r4.claim: The rising moon is the heart reaching its station above the soul and receiving disclosures of realities; God manifests its illumination through the names al-ʿAlīm and al-Ḥakīm.
QASHANI:6:76-77/r4.anchor: قمر القلب بازغا بوصوله إلى مقام القلب وطلوعه من أفق النفس

QASHANI:6:76-77/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:76-77/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:76-77/r5.claim: When the moon sets, the heart recognizes its light is received from the spirit and may disappear in the darkness of the soul and its attributes, so it turns toward the spirit's manifestation.
QASHANI:6:76-77/r5.anchor: نوره مستفاد من شمس الروح وإنه قد يتغيب في ظلمة النفس وصفاتها فيحتجب بها

QASHANI:6:76-77/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:76-77/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:76-77/r6.claim: Abraham asks for guidance to the divine light lest he join those, like Christians, who stop at luminous inner veils.
QASHANI:6:76-77/r6.anchor: الذين يحتجبون بالبواطن عنه كالنصارى الواقفين مع الحجب النورانية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r1.speaker: الأزهري؛ الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r1.claim: Bāzigh means beginning to rise and spreading light; al-Azhari connects it to splitting, as the moon’s light cleaves darkness, with related uses for a tooth emerging and blood flowing.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r1.anchor: أي مبتدأ في الطلوع منتشر الضوء ولعله كما قال الازهري مأخوذ من البزغ وهو الشق كأنه بنوره يشق الظلمة شقا ويقال بزغ الناب إذا ظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r2.claim: The verse’s apparent sequence has the moon seen after the star has set, and “this is my Lord” follows the same argumentative pattern as before.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r2.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : ( قال هذا ربي ( جواب لما وهو على طرز الكلام السابق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r3.claim: The prayer asks God to guide Abraham to the inescapable path of truth, since none of the things he had seen could be divine.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r3.anchor: فان شيئا مما زايته لا يصلح للربوبية وهذا مبالغة منه عليه السلام في النصفة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the conditional prayer as a fair-minded warning that whoever takes the moon as a god, although it sets like the stars, is astray.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r4.anchor: وفيه كما قال الزمخشري تنبيه لقومه على أن من اتخذ القمر إلها وهو نظير الكواكب في الأفول فهو ضال

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r5.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Munir says this is a clearer and stronger insinuation that the people are astray than the earlier “I do not love those that set.”
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r5.anchor: كما ابن المنير أصرح وأقوى من قوله أولا ( لا أحب الآفلين )

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r6.claim: Abraham escalates only after the first proof has softened resistance; he delays explicit accusation until sure the people will hear the argument through, then disavows their shirk in the next verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r6.anchor: وإنما ترقى عليه السلام إلى ذلك لأن الخصوم قد قامت عليهم بالاستدلال الاول حجة فانسوا بالقدح في معتقدهم ولو قيل هذا في الاول فلعلهم كانوا ينفرون ولا يصغون إلى الاستدلال

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r7.claim: This wording and what follows show Abraham was arguing with his people, not seeking guidance for himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r7.anchor: وفي هذه الجملة دليل من غير وجه على أن استدلاله عليه السلام ليس لنفسه بل كان محاجة لقومه وكذا ما سيأتي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r8.claim: An alternative takes the prayer as Abraham’s inability to find truth by himself and a request for God’s aid; another reads the next verse as certainty gained from the proof, but Al-Alusi says both are far from the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r8.anchor: وحمل هذا على أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام استعجز نفسه فاستعان بربه عز وجل في درك الحق وما سيأتي على أنه إشارة إلى حصول اليقين من الدليل خلاف الظاهر جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r9.claim: Al-Alusi notes that certainty gained by reasoning would still be compatible with Abraham debating his people.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r9.anchor: على أنه قيل : إن حصول اليقين من الدليل لا ينافي المحاجة مع القوم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r10.speaker: شيخ الاسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r10.claim: Shaykh al-Islam’s astronomical reconstruction places Abraham west of a high mountain that hid the star and moon near midday, with the star initially near him and the eastern horizon visible.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p200#2/r10.anchor: أنه عليه السلام كان إذا ذاك في موضع كان في جانبه الغربي جبل شامخ يستتر به الكوكب والقمر وقت الظهر من النهار أو بعده بقليل وكان الكوكب قريبا منه وافقه الشرقي مكشوف أولا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162#2/r2.claim: The prayer for guidance means asking God to keep Abraham firm in guidance, not that he lacked it; prophets ask God to preserve their faith, as Abraham also prayed regarding himself and his children.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162#2/r2.anchor: قيل: لئن لم يثبتني على الهدى، ليس أنه لم يكن مهتديا، والأنبياء لم يزالوا يسألون الله تعالى الثبات على الإيمان،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162#2/r3.claim: Being among the misguided means being away from guidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p162#2/r3.anchor: {لأكونن من القوم الضالين} أي: عن الهدى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:77/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:77/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:77/r2.claim: Abraham admits his inability and asks his Lord for help in attaining truth, which is reached only through divine enabling.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:77/r2.anchor: استعجز نفسه واستعان بربه في درك الحق، فإنه لا يهتدي إليه إلا بتوفيقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:77/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:77/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:77/r3.claim: He guides his people and shows that the moon's changing state disqualifies it as a deity, so anyone who worships it is astray.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:77/r3.anchor: إرشادا لقومه وتنبيها لهم على أن القمر أيضا لتغير حاله لا يصلح للألوهية، وأن من اتخذه إلها فهو ضال.

SULAMI:v1p205/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p205/r5.claim: Ibn Ata reads the first statement as distinguishing Abraham from his people and the next as seeking increased guidance; once the proof was established, Abraham disavowed their associations.
SULAMI:v1p205/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في هذه الآية ﴿ هذا ربي ﴾ قال : كان الأول تفريقا للقوم ، والثاني مسأله الإزدياد للهداية

SULAMI:v1p205/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p205/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p205/r7.claim: One account traces Abraham's passage from darkness and compulsion through lights of lordship and awe, to effacement of human traits, subsistence in the Everlasting, and disavowal of association.
SULAMI:v1p205/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لما أظلم عليه الكون وعمى عن الإختيار وألجأه الإضطرار إلى النفس

SULAMI:v1p206/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p206/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p206/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says Abraham feared misguidance if God did not establish him in the guidance he had witnessed, since looking to himself would leave him in his own attributes.
SULAMI:v1p206/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : لئن لم يقمني ربي على الهداية التي شاهدتها بإعلام بواديه

SULAMI:v1p206/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p206/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p206/r2.claim: Sahl takes the plea to mean that without God's help Abraham would have fallen into the same error as his people.
SULAMI:v1p206/r2.anchor: وقال سهل في هذه الآية : لئن لم يهدني ربي بمعونة منه لأكونن مثلكم في الضلالة

SULAMI:v1p206/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p206/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p206/r3.claim: Some say Abraham asks God to increase his guidance and keep him firm upon it.
SULAMI:v1p206/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لئن لم يزدني هدى ولم يثبتني على الهداية

SULAMI:v1p206/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p206/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p206/r4.claim: Some say he asks for further guidance lest he worship as his people do; after proving their objects were no gods, he returned to his homeland and disavowed their associations.
SULAMI:v1p206/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لئن لم يكرمني بمزيد الهداية لأكونن كما أنتم في عبادتكم

SULAMI:v1p206/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p206/r6.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p206/r6.claim: Al-Wasiti says the servant supplies the invocation, while guidance comes from God.
SULAMI:v1p206/r6.anchor: قال الواسطي : منى الدعوة ومن الله الهداية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r1.speaker: الأزهري
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r1.claim: Al-Azhari explains the moon's first appearance with bazigh and says the word may derive from splitting, as its light cleaves the darkness.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r1.anchor: بازغا } أي طالعا أول طلوعه ؛ قال الأزهري : كأنه مأخوذ من البزغ الذي هو الشق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r2.claim: The moon's statement this is my Lord follows Abraham's earlier rhetorical tactic.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r2.anchor: قال هذا ربي } دأبه في الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r3.claim: The star's setting had already unsettled the audience because they heard it was subject to events, so Abraham emphasizes his response.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r3.anchor: تأمل أن الكوكب محل الحوادث بالأفول قد طرق أسماعهم فخالج صدورهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r4.claim: Abraham's plea shows guidance comes from God, not from someone else, the mere display of already-present proofs, or knowledge of inference he already possessed.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r4.anchor: فدل ذلك على أن الهداية ليست إلى غيره , ولا تحمل على نصب الأدلة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r5.claim: This is a stronger and more explicit repudiation of the heavenly bodies' divinity than the first statement, while remaining tactful toward opponents.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p659/r5.anchor: فكانت هذه أشد من الأولى وأقرب إلى التصريح بنفي الربوبية عن الكواكب

TUSTARI:6:77/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:77/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:77/r1.claim: Abraham asks that his guidance continue without interruption.
TUSTARI:6:77/r1.anchor: يعني لئن لم يدم لي الهداية

TUSTARI:6:77/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:77/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:77/r2.claim: Abraham's way is generosity and disavowal of everything besides God, relying on no one else in any state.
TUSTARI:6:77/r2.anchor: كانت ملة إبراهيم عليه السلام السخاوة، وحالة التبري من كل شيء سوى الله تعالى

TUSTARI:6:77/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:77/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TUSTARI:6:77/r3.claim: When Gabriel asked whether he had a need, Abraham replied that he had no need of Gabriel, illustrating reliance on God alone.
TUSTARI:6:77/r3.anchor: ألا تراه حين قال جبريل عليه السلام: هل لك حاجة؟ قال: أما إليك فلا

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abraham worshipped the moon until it disappeared.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : فلما راى القمر بازغا قال هذا ربي ، قال : فعبده حتى غاب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham emerged at the end of the month, so he had not seen the moon before the star.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : وخرج في اخر الشهر ، فلذلك لم ير القمر قبل الكوكب

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says that late that night Abraham saw the moon.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : وخرج في اخر الشهر ، فلذلك لم ير القمر قبل الكوكب فلما كان اخر الليل راى القمر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r4.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the moon’s setting as its disappearance and reports Abraham’s plea that without his Lord’s guidance he would be among the astray.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1329/r4.anchor: وبه ، عن السدى : فلما افل ، يقول : غاب قال لئن لم يهدني ربي لاكونن من القوم الضالين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r9.claim: Bazighan means the first appearance or rising of these celestial lights.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r9.anchor: البزوغ في هذه الأنوار: أول الطلوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r11.claim: Yahdinī means ‘guide me’; the wording supports those who place the episode in Abraham’s childhood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r11.anchor: ويهدني يرشدني وهذا اللفظ يؤيد قول من قال: النازلة في حال الصغر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r12.claim: The ‘astray people’ intended here are worshippers of created things such as idols, although the term for straying is broader in general.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p313#2/r12.anchor: و «القوم الضالون» عبدة المخلوقات، كالأصنام وغيرها وإن كان الضلال أعم من هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r5.claim: The plea for guidance does not prove earlier doubt: prophets continually seek guidance and protection from error, as Abraham asked God to keep him and his children from idol worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p73/r5.anchor: فما زال الأنبياء يسألون الهدى ويتضرعون في دفع الضلال عنهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75#2/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75#2/r1.claim: The moon is named for its whiteness; الأقمر means white and a ليلة قمراء is a bright night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة سمي القمر قمرا لبياضه والأقمر الأبيض وليلة قمراء أي مضيئة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75#2/r3.claim: The plea for guidance means asking God to keep one firm upon guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p75#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى ﴿ لئن لم يهدني ﴾ لئن لم يثبتني على الهدى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r6.claim: Bāzigh means rising; Abraham describes the sun as luminous and rising, and “greater” as greater in size and brighter than the star and moon.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r6.anchor: فلما رأى القمر بازغا} أي: طالعا {قال هذا ربي فلما أفل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir understands Abraham's scene as contemplation and favors that reading because Abraham says that without his Lord's guidance he would be among the astray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r8.anchor: فروى ابن جرير من طريق علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس ما يقتضي أنه مقام نظر، واختاره ابن جرير مستدلا بقوله: {لئن لم يهدني ربي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r9.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r9.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Abraham spoke after emerging from the cave where his mother had given birth and hidden him from Nimrod, who ordered boys killed after hearing of a child who would end his rule.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p291/r9.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: قال ذلك حين خرج من السرب الذي ولدته فيه أمه، حين تخوفت عليه النمرود بن كنعان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292/r3.claim: The planets' fixed, God-governed paths and lack of self-direction disqualify them from divinity; Abraham demonstrates this successively for Venus, the moon, and the sun.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292/r3.anchor: لأنها مسخرة مقدرة بسير معين، لا تزيغ عنه يمينا ولا شمالا ولا تملك لنفسها تصرفا، بل هي جرم من الأجرام خلقها الله منيرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292#2/r1.claim: The Prophet reports that every newborn is born upon the fitra, supporting Ibn Kathir's rejection of the idea that Abraham was still searching for true belief.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p292#2/r1.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيحين، عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "كل مولود يولد على الفطرة" (1)

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وورش عن نافع
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Warsh from Nāfiʿ open the rāʾ and kasra the hamza after the alif in raʾā throughout.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وورش عن نافع: رأى بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة بعد الألف حيث كان

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī generally kasra both rāʾ and hamza, with differences before k or h and before a connecting alif.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بكسرهما

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r3.speaker: يحيى عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r3.claim: Yaḥyā from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim transmits the same reading as Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī in the specified environment.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r3.anchor: وروى يحيى عن أبي بكر عن عاصم مثل قراءة حمزة والكسائي

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r4.speaker: حمزة ويحيى عن أبي بكر ونصيرا عن الكسائي
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r4.claim: When raʾā is followed by an alif of connection, these readers kasra the rāʾ and open the hamza.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r4.anchor: فإن حمزة ويحيى عن أبي بكر ونصيرا عن الكسائي يكسرون الراء ويفتحون الهمزة

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r5.claim: The other readers open both vowels; all agree on the fatḥa in raʾūka and raʾathum, and imāla follows the yāʾ which drops before a connecting alif.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الباقون جميع ذلك بفتح الراء والهمزة، واتفقوا في رأوك ورأتهم بالفتح

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r10.claim: The moon is called hilāl during the first three nights, then qamar for the rest of the month; qamar is named for its whiteness, as in the phrase ḥimār aqmar.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r10.anchor: ويسمى ثلاث ليال من أول الشهر هلالا، ثم قمرا إلى آخر الشهر، وسمي قمرا لبياضه

JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r11.claim: Bāzigh means appearing or rising; the root also describes a horse's incision to let blood, the sun's rising, and a tooth emerging.
JISHUMI:v3p2294#2/r11.anchor: والبازغ: البارز الطالع، بزغ يبزغ بزوغا، ونجوم بوازغ

JISHUMI:v3p2296/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r4.claim: In the Abraham narrative, the first lām is an oath and the lām in la-akūnanna answers it.
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r4.anchor: قلنا: الأول: حلف من القسم، والثانية جواب لها إذا صارت حلفا من القسم فأجيب بجوابه

JISHUMI:v3p2296/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r8.claim: The passage follows God's signs shown to Abraham and explains his reasoning and recognition of truth.
JISHUMI:v3p2296/r8.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر الآيات التي أراها الله تعالى إبراهيم بين كيف استدل، وكيف اعترف بالحق، فقال سبحانه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r2.claim: Bāziġ means rising; the same word describes the sun when it rises.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r2.anchor: أي طالعا , وكذلك بزغت الشمس أي طلعت

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r3.claim: Setting proves celestial bodies cannot be worshipped because their change shows they are governed and originated, and what has that quality cannot be a deity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137/r3.anchor: لأن تغيرها بالأفول دليل على أنها مدبرة محدثة , وما كان بهذه الصفة استحال أن يكون إلها معبودا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#3/r2.claim: By saying this to his people, Abraham points out that whoever takes the moon as a god is astray.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#3/r2.anchor: نبه قومه على أن من اتخذ القمر إلها فهو ضال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#3/r3.claim: He argues from setting rather than rising, although both are changes of state, because setting is a clearer transition through concealment and disappearance.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p331#3/r3.anchor: و إنما احتج عليهم بالأفول دون البزوع وكلاهما انتقال من حال إلى حال لأن الاحتجاج به أظهر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r1.claim: Bāzighan means rising; the root evokes light splitting darkness, and it also names a veterinary incision that releases an animal's blood.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r1.anchor: أي طالعا. يقال: بزغ القمر إذا ابتدأ في الطلوع، والبزغ الشق كأنه يشق بنوره الظلمة ومنه بزغ البيطار الدابة إذا أسال دمها.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r2.claim: Abraham's request for guidance means asking God to keep him firm in guidance; he was already guided, as in the prayer 'Guide us to the straight path.'
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r2.anchor: وفي التنزيل: «إهدنا الصراط المستقيم» أي ثبتنا على الهداية.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r3.claim: The statement may have occurred during a period of inquiry, or it may ask for firmness given the rational possibility of a change, as Shuʿayb says that return depends on God's will.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:77/r3.anchor: وقد كان مهتديا فيكون جرى هذا في مهلة النظر، أو سأل التثبيت لإمكان الجواز العقلي كما قال شعيب:

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r2.claim: Some map star, moon, and sun to sense, imagination and estimation, and intellect; these finite faculties are ruled by the governor of the world.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r2.anchor: ومن الناس من حمل الكوكب على الحس والقمر على الخيال والوهم ، والشمس على العقل

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r8.claim: Bāzigh means the moon or sun has begun to rise; al-Azhari explains the word through splitting, as its light cleaves darkness.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r8.anchor: قال الأزهري : كأنه مأخوذ في البزغ وهو الشق كأنه بنوره يشق الظلمة شقا

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r9.claim: Abraham applies the same consideration to the moon as he did to the star.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r9.anchor: أنه اعتبر في القمر مثل ما اعتبر في الكوكب

RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r10.claim: Guidance comes only from God; here it cannot mean enabling, removing obstacles, or presenting proofs, since those were already present and the requested guidance exceeds them.
RAZI-FULL:v13p45#2/r10.anchor: الهداية التي كان يطلبها بعد حصول تلك الأشياء لا بد وأن تكون زائدة عليها

RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p46/r1.claim: Abraham’s attribution of guidance to God here, in 26:78, and in his prayer of 14:35 clearly establishes the author’s theological position.

SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r1.speaker: ابن ذكوان
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r1.claim: When رأى is attached to a pronoun, Ibn Dhakwān has two routes in the cited examples; the other readers retain their previously stated rules.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r1.anchor: فابن ذكوان عنه وجهان، والباقون على أصولهم المتقدمة.

SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r2.claim: For رأى forms whose alif is permanently absent, such as رأتهم and رأوا, no imāla applies; the same holds when the alif changes to yāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r2.anchor: فلا إمالة في شيء منه، وكذا ما انقلبت ألفه ياء نحو: رأيت ثم رأيت

SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r3.claim: When alif is omitted in liaison only to avoid two adjacent sukūns, it returns at pause; readers differ over imāla in forms such as رأى القمر and رأى الشمس.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r3.anchor: قسم حذفت ألفه لالتقاء الساكنين وصلا، وتعود وقفا نحو: رأى القمر

SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r4.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r4.claim: Ḥamza, Abū Bakr, and al-Sūsī in one route always incline the rāʾ alone in this form; Abū Bakr and al-Sūsī also incline the hamza with it in one route.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r4.anchor: فأمال الراء وحدها من غير خلاف حمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم والسوسي بخلاف عنه وحده.

SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r5.claim: At pause the alif returns, so the verb follows the rules for a form not followed by a consonant; inclining the rāʾ is conventionally attributed to imāla of the hamza, though the alif is the actual target because it derives from yāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r5.anchor: أما إذا وقفت فإن الألف ترجع لعدم المقتضي لحذفها، وحكم هذا الفعل حينئذ حكم ما لم يتصل به ساكن

SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r6.claim: Ibn Dhakwān’s distinction depends on attachment: the alif is farther from the word’s end with an attached pronoun and is not inclined; when it is deleted only temporarily, some retain imāla of the hamza alone while others also incline the rāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r6.anchor: وأما تفصيل ابن ذكوان بالنسبة إلى اتصاله بالضمير وعدمه فوجهه أن الفعل لما اتصل بالضمير بعدت ألفه من الطرف فلم تمل

SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r7.claim: كوكب means a star and has the variant form كوكبة; al-Rāghib says a star is called كوكب specifically when it appears.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r7.anchor: والكوكب: النجم، ويقال فيه كوكبة، وقال الراغب: " لا يقال فيه أي في النجم كوكب

SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r8.speaker: الصغاني
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r8.claim: Al-Ṣaghānī derives كوكب from وكب, treating its initial kāf as extra; he says the lexeme belongs under وكب despite al-Jawharī’s and al-Layth’s quadriliteral analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77/r8.anchor: قاله الشيخ رضي الدين الصغاني، قال رحمه الله: " حق كوكب أن يذكر في مادة " وكب "

SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r1.claim: بازغا is a circumstantial accusative describing the moon. بزوغ means rising; the verb can be intransitive or transitive, first of a veterinarian letting an animal’s blood and then of the blood flowing, before the word generalized to rising.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r1.anchor: بازغا }: حال من القمر. والبزوغ: الطلوع، يقال: بزغ بفتح الزاي يبزغ بضمها بزوغا، ويستعمل قاصرا ومتعديا،

SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r2.claim: The noun’s later usage includes a child’s or camel’s tooth emerging, by analogy with the original sense.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r2.anchor: ثم قيل لكل طلوع: بزوغ، ومنه: بزغ ناب الصبي والبعير تشبيها بذلك،

SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r3.claim: Several etymologies are reported for القمر: its whiteness and spread of light, or its overcoming the stars’ light and taking it for itself; القمراء means moonlight, and الأقمر is a donkey of the moonlit night’s color.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r3.anchor: والقمر معروف، سمي بذلك لبياضه وانتشار ضوئه، والأقمر: الحمار الذي على لون الليلة القمراء، والقمراء ضوء القمر،

SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r4.claim: الليالي القمر are the bright nights in which the moon’s light lasts until morning; some linguists reserve قمر for after the third night, call it هلال before that, and بدر from the third night after the tenth through the fifteenth.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r4.anchor: والليالي القمر: ليالي تدور القمر وهي الليالي البيض، لأن ضوء القمر يستمر فيها إلى الصباح،

SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r5.claim: The verb قمرت فلانا can mean tricking someone away from something and is likened to a water-skin becoming sealed in moonlight.
SAMIN-DURR:6:77#2/r5.anchor: ويقال: قمرت فلانا كذا أي خدعته عنه، وكأنه مأخوذ من قمرت القربة فسدت بالقمراء.

TAB-FULL:v9p356/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the kingdom shown to Abraham as the sun, moon, and stars, and reports that Abraham worshipped each celestial body until it set before declaring disavowal of what his people associated with God.
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السموات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين} : يعني به: الشمس والقمر والنجوم

TAB-FULL:v9p356/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r2.claim: Qatādah says the star’s setting taught Abraham that his Lord is everlasting and does not disappear; at the sun he saw a creation greater and brighter than the first two.
TAB-FULL:v9p356/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: {فلما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا قال هذا ربي فلما أفل قال لا أحب الآفلين} [الأنعام: 76] : علم أن ربه دائم لا يزول

TAB-FULL:v9p362/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r1.claim: When the moon appeared, Abraham called it his lord; when it set, he asked his Lord to guide and enable him to affirm divine unity, lest he join those who missed truth and worshipped other than God.
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r1.anchor: فلما طلع القمر فرآه إبراهيم طالعا، وهو بزوغه، يقال منه: بزغت الشمس تبزغ بزوغا

TAB-FULL:v9p362/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r2.claim: Bazagha means to rise or appear, whether of the sun or moon.
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r2.anchor: يقال منه: بزغت الشمس تبزغ بزوغا، إذا طلعت، وكذلك القمر.

TAB-FULL:v9p362/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r3.claim: The request for guidance means asking God to enable him to attain the truth in affirming His unity.
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r3.anchor: {لئن لم يهدني ربي} [الأنعام: 77] ويوفقني لإصابة الحق في توحيده

TAB-FULL:v9p362/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r4.claim: The misguided are those who missed the truth and guidance and worshipped someone other than God.
TAB-FULL:v9p362/r4.anchor: أي من القوم الذين أخطئوا الحق في ذلك، فلم يصيبوا الهدى، وعبدوا غير الله.

TABATABAI:6:76-78/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r1.claim: After debating his father and people about idols, Abraham turns to their astral objects, successively saying “this is my lord” of the star, moon, and sun, with the sun “greater.”
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r1.anchor: ثم إنه عليه السلام بعد الفراغ مما حاج به أباه آزر وقومه في أمر الأصنام يشتغل بأربابها وهي الكوكب والقمر والشمس

TABATABAI:6:76-78/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads the demonstratives as words of someone unfamiliar with the star, moon, and sun, who knows only that people worship and sacrifice to them.
TABATABAI:6:76-78/r2.anchor: وهذه التعبيرات أيضا تعبير من كأنه لم ير كوكبا ولا قمرا ولا شمسا

TABATABAI:6:79/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:79/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:79/r2.claim: Abraham lived apart from his father's society, joined him, questioned and refuted idol worship, challenged his people, then successively tested the star, moon, and sun before returning to pure monotheism.
TABATABAI:6:79/r2.anchor: إنما عاش قبل ذلك في معزل من الجو الذي كان يعيش فيه أبوه وقومه ولم يكن يعرف ما يعرفه معاشر المجتمعين من تفاصيل شؤون أجزاء الكون

TABATABAI:6:79/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:79/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:79/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī thinks the sequence likely unfolded over about two days and one night.
TABATABAI:6:79/r3.anchor: وكأنه تم له ذلك في يومين وليلة بينهما تقريبا على ما سنبين إن شاء الله تعالى

TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r1.claim: Buzūgh means rising; the crescent is called hilāl during the month's first three nights and then qamar for the rest of the month, a name associated with its whiteness.
TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r1.anchor: والبزوغ الطلوع يقال بزغت الشمس إذا طلعت ويسمى ثلاث ليال من أول الشهر الهلال

TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r2.claim: The adjective aqmar means white, as in a white camel.
TABRISI:6:76-79#2/r2.anchor: وإنما يسمى قمرا لبياضه وحمار أقمر أبيض

TABRISI:6:76-79#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:76-79#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:76-79#3/r2.claim: As the moon rises, its size, brilliance, and spreading light prompt Abraham's provisional statement; its setting shows that it cannot be divine, so he asks God to guide him lest he join those astray.
TABRISI:6:76-79#3/r2.anchor: وعلم أنه لا يجوز أن يكون ذلك صفة الإله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r1.claim: Bazagha means that the moon begins to rise; for the sun it is the first appearance of its rising, and stars are likewise called rising.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r1.anchor: يقال: بزغ القمر: إذا ابتدأ في الطلوع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r2.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r2.claim: Al-Azharī derives bazagha from splitting: moonlight cleaves the darkness, just as a veterinarian splits an animal's hair at the incision site.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r2.anchor: قال الأزهري (¬6): (كأنه مأخوذ من البزغ، وهو الشق، كأنه يشق بنوره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r3.speaker: الطرماح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r3.claim: Al-Ṭirimmāḥ's line uses bazgh in the veterinarian's sense of making an incision in an animal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r3.anchor: قال الطرماح: كبزغ البيطر الثقف رهص الكوادن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r4.claim: Abraham considered the moon and sun as he had considered the star, and his argument against his people was the same.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r4.anchor: فإن إبراهيم عليه السلام اعتبر في القمر والشمس مثل ما اعتبر في النجم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r5.claim: Abraham's plea for guidance does not imply he lacked guidance; it asks God to keep him firm, as prophets know they could not be guided without God and continually ask Him for this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p248/r5.anchor: لا يوجب أنه لم يكن مهتديا؛ لأن معناه: لئن لم يثبتني على الهدى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:77-79/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:77-79/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:77-79/r1.claim: The moon's rising gave Abraham the same argument he had made against the star, and he used it for the sun as well.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:77-79/r1.anchor: فاحتج عليهم في القمر والشمس بمثل ما احتج به عليهم في الكوكب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:77-79/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:77-79/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:77-79/r2.claim: Abraham's plea for guidance means asking God to keep him firm upon guidance.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:77-79/r2.anchor: أي: لئن لم يثبتني على الهدى.

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r13.claim: When the dawn of realization came and the suns of gnosis rose, no room remained for seeking, possibility, or suspicion, so Abraham disavowed what his people associated.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r13.anchor: فلم يبق للطلب مكان ، ولا للتجويز حكم ، ولا للتهمة قرار

QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r14.claim: An alternative reading has Abraham first see created signs through God, then see things as belonging to and coming from God, and finally behold them effaced in God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p299/r14.anchor: كان يلاحظ الآثار والأغيار بالله ، ثم كان يرى الأشياء لله ومن الله

ITQAN:v1p19/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p19/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p19/r1.claim: The author recounts that early scholars had not compiled Qurʾanic sciences as they had hadith; al-Kāfījī showed him a very brief work, which did not satisfy his inquiry.
ITQAN:v1p19/r1.anchor: ولقد كنت في زمان الطلب أتعجب من المتقدمين إذ لم يدونوا كتابا في أنواع علوم القرآن

ITQAN:v1p19/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p19/r2.speaker: الكافيجي
ITQAN:v1p19/r2.claim: Al-Kāfījī’s work had two chapters: definitions of tafsīr, taʾwīl, Qurʾān, sūra, and verse; then conditions for opinion-based exegesis, followed by scholar-student etiquette.
ITQAN:v1p19/r2.anchor: فإذا هو صغير الحجم جدا وحاصل ما فيه بابان الأول في ذكر معنى التفسير والتأويل والقرآن والسورة والآية والثاني في شروط القول فيه بالرأي

ITQAN:v1p19/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p19/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p19/r3.claim: Al-Balqīnī introduced the author to his brother Jalāl al-Dīn’s Mawaqiʿ al-ʿUlūm, which the author praised for its elegant organization and treatment.
ITQAN:v1p19/r3.anchor: ثم أوقفني شيخنا شيخ مشايخ الإسلام قاضي القضاة وخلاصة الأنام حامل لواء المذهب المطلبي علم الدين البلقيني رحمه الله تعالى على كتاب في ذلك لأخيه قاضي القضاة جلال الدين سماه مواقع العلوم من مواقع النجوم فرأيته تأليفا لطيفا ومجموعا ظريفا

ITQAN:v1p19/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p19/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p19/r4.claim: The work’s first division covers locations and circumstances of revelation: Meccan-Medinan, travel-residence, night-day, seasonal, bed-sleep, causes, and first and last revelations.
ITQAN:v1p19/r4.anchor: الأمر الأول مواطن النزول وأوقاته ووقائعه وفي ذلك اثنا عشر نوعا المكي المدني السفري الحضري الليلي النهاري الصيفي الشتائي الفراشي النومي أسباب النزول أول ما نزل آخر ما نزل

ITQAN:v1p19/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p19/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p19/r5.claim: Its second division concerns transmission: mutawātir, solitary and anomalous readings, the Prophet’s readings, transmitters, and memorisers.
ITQAN:v1p19/r5.anchor: الأمر الثاني السند وهو ستة أنواع المتواتر الآحاد الشاذ قراءات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الرواة الحفاظ

ITQAN:v1p19/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p19/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p19/r6.claim: Its third division concerns performance, listing pauses, beginnings, imāla, lengthening, hamza easing, and assimilation.
ITQAN:v1p19/r6.anchor: الأمر الثالث الأداء وهو ستة أنواع الوقف الابتداء الإمالة المد تخفيف الهمزة الإدغام

BURHAN:v2p134/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p134/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p134/r1.claim: Abraham’s rejection of setting stars supports the Prophet’s report that the source of fitna and disbelief is toward the east; repentance’s door opens from the west.
BURHAN:v2p134/r1.anchor: ما يبين تصديق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله رأس الفتنة والكفر نحو المشرق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r1.claim: Abraham’s statement about the star is a staged argument: he feigns the community’s reverence to gain their trust, then shows that a setting star cannot be God and applies the lesson to moon and sun without provocation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r1.anchor: يريد: أن يستدرجهم بهذا القول، ويعرفهم خطأهم، وجهلهم في تعظيمهم شأن النجوم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r3.claim: The author compares Abraham’s strategy to a ḥawārī who feigned devotion to an idol, exposed its inability to help against an enemy, and then led its worshippers to pray to God, who delivered them.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r3.anchor: ومثل هذا: الحواري حين ورد على قوم يعبدون (بدا) لهم فأظهر تعظيمه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r4.speaker: من الناس
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r4.claim: Some claim Abraham was then in error and confusion; Ibn Qutayba rejects this because God protected and purified him, citing his sound heart and exegetes who say he never associated anything with God.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p202/r4.anchor: ومن الناس من يذهب إلى أن إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم، كان في تلك الحال على ضلال وحيرة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p201/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p201/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p201/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba places Abraham in an age of astrology and divination, when people revered stars and claimed they foretold hidden events; Nimrod ordered newborns killed after astrologers predicted Abraham’s birth.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p201/r1.anchor: عصر نجوم وكهانة، وإنما أمر نمروذ

NASHR:v1p484/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p484/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p484/r1.claim: In raʾā al-qamar, the fixed alif is the written shape of hamza and the following alif is omitted for abbreviation due to identical letters, not to avoid two sukūns.
NASHR:v1p484/r1.anchor: فإن الألف فيه هي صورة الهمزة، والألف بعدها حذفت اختصارا
